H5329: properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent
H4210: properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes
H1732: David, the youngest son of Jesse
H6030: properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce
H3068: Jehovah, Jewish national name of God
H3117: a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb)
H6869: tightness (i.e. figuratively, trouble); transitively, a female rival:
H7682: to be (causatively, make) lofty, especially inaccessible; by implication, safe, strong; used literally and figuratively
H8034: an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character
H430: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
H7971: to send away, for, or out (in a great variety of applications)
H6944: a sacred place or thing; rarely abstract, sanctity
H6726: Tsijon (as a permanent capital), a mountain of Jerusalem
H2142: properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention; to be male
H3605: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
H4503: a donation; euphemistically, tribute; specifically a sacrificial offering (usually bloodless and voluntary)
H5930: a step or (collectively, stairs, as ascending); usually a holocaust (as going up in smoke)
H1878: to be fat; transitively, to fatten (or regard as fat); specifically to anoint; figuratively, to satisfy; to remove (fat) ashes (of sacrifices)
H5414: to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.)
H3824: the heart (as the most interior organ);
H6098: advice; by implication, plan; also prudence
H4390: to fill or (intransitively) be full of, in a wide application (literally and figuratively)
H7442: properly, to creak (or emit a stridulous sound), i.e. to shout (usually for joy)
H3444: something saved, i.e. (abstractly) deliverance; hence, aid, victory, prosperity
H1713: to flaunt, i.e. raise a flag; figuratively, to be conspicuous
H6258: at this time, whether adverb, conjunction or expletive
H3045: to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)
H3588: (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed
H3467: properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor
H4899: anointed; usually a consecrated person (as a king, priest, or saint); specifically, the Messiah
H8064: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
H1369: force (literally or figuratively); by implication, valor, victory
H3225: the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south
H7393: a vehicle; by implication, a team; by extension, cavalry; by analogy a rider, i.e. the upper millstone
H5483: a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight)
H3766: to bend the knee; by implication, to sink, to prostrate
H5307: to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative)
H6965: to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)
H5749: to duplicate or repeat; by implication, to protest, testify (as by reiteration); intensively, to encompass, restore (as a sort of reduplication)
H7121: to call out to (i.e. properly, address by name, but used in a wide variety of applications)
